research_method.claude: Centralized CI/CD (IDP) architecture proposal evaluated by a retrospective observational case study: before/after comparison (decentralized 7 months vs. centralized 3 months) with DORA Lead Time, CFR and MTTR from Azure DevOps REST API pipeline logs and up to 39 recorded incident meetings; descriptive means, no statistical tests
research_method.nlm: Retrospective observational case study (mixed methods): pipeline execution logs via Azure DevOps REST API and up to 39 recorded Teams incident meetings; DORA Lead Time, CFR, MTTR compared between decentralized (7 months) and centralized (3 months) phases
research_method.value: Centralized CI/CD architecture (Internal Developer Platform) proposal evaluated by a retrospective observational case study; before/after comparison of decentralized (7 months) vs. centralized (3 months) phases using DORA Lead Time (pipeline duration), CFR and MTTR computed from Azure DevOps REST API pipeline-run logs and up to 39 recorded Microsoft Teams incident meetings; 30 microservices; descriptive comparison
research_method.note: Absence of statistical tests noted by Claude only (not contradicted).

evidence.quote: We conducted a retrospective observational case study on a large enterprise that transitioned to this exact architecture which allows us to directly perform a comparison against their previous decentralized approach.

This study uses a mixed-methods approach to evaluate the transition to a centralized CI/CD architecture. The gathered data was a combination of both historical pipeline execution logs and recorded incident meetings.
To track incidents, we collected up to 39 recorded Microsoft Teams meetings where DevOps engineers collaborated to fix deployment failures during the migration period.

The migration spanned a 10 month period ranging from April 2025 to February 2026. While the company housed over approximately 300 services, there were only 30 of them successfully migrated into the production environment.
Data during the transition period between October and November 2025 was excluded from the calculations
By analyzing the engineering effort across 30 microservices, we have evaluated its impact by three DORA metrics such as Lead Time, Mean Time to Restore (MTTR), and Change Failure Rate (CFR).
Our findings show that the centralized approach resulted in the reduction of Lead Time by 77.9% and CFR by 88.2%. On the contrary, the MTTR saw a significant increase by 63.0%
The centralized architecture experienced an increase in the number of successful deployments from 143 to 161 compared to the decentralized architecture
